references.text: God tells Moses that He has seen the suffering of His people in Egypt and has come to rescue them, which points forward to Jesus' mission to save the lost sheep of the house of Israel
The prophet Isaiah describes how all who are like sheep have gone astray, emphasizing the need for a Savior, as Jesus refers to His mission for the house of Israel

Hosea prophesies that the children of Israel will be like the sand by the sea, which cannot be measured or numbered, and that they will be called 'children of God,' reflecting Jesus' focus on the house of Israel
Jesus sends out His twelve disciples and instructs them to go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, which directly corresponds with His statement in Matthew 15:24
Jesus explains that He has come to save what was lost, reflecting His mission as expressed in Matthew 15:24
